verdict.probe_answer: The memo correctly verifies the Python-only double-capture mechanism with precise file:line citations, correctly maps the resolver/CPG blast radius, and correctly hedges on JS/TS (recommending a canary rather than assuming a fix is needed there) — matching the settled outcome's Python-only scoping and JS/TS caution. However, its core architectural recommendation is inverted: it proposes making the inner `function_definition` canonical and dropping the `decorated_definition` wrapper, while the shipped fix (#132) did the opposite — wrapper-canonical, dropping the inner. The memo even flags in its own Risks section that dropping the wrapper loses decorator-line coverage, which is plausibly exactly why the team chose wrapper-canonical instead — meaning following this memo as written would likely have required a reversal once span/decorator-coverage issues surfaced.
verdict.rationale: Scope (Python-only, extraction-level canonicalization, defer decorator semantics/JS-TS unless canary-proven) is well-calibrated and matches the shipped slice's shape and size. But the single most decisive design choice — which node becomes the canonical FunctionId — is the opposite of what was vindicated, so the memo would not have prevented rework; a team implementing it would likely have hit the decorator-span/coverage problem the memo itself anticipated and then had to flip to wrapper-canonical, matching the real commit history (inventory keeps decorated wrapper, unwrap_decorated used only for field reads).
